name: fresh-review
description: Architect-first code review with enforced producer/reviewer context separation. Every run starts with an architecture risk tier — low, medium, or high — set by a context-isolated pass that reads the code alone. Low (no architecture change) runs the code review on its own. Medium and high get a short brief: a before and an after diagram in the domain's own DDD language (bounded contexts, aggregates, services, events, outside systems — no class names or code), at most two paragraphs on what changed, and the PR's own screenshots when the UI changed (the app is never launched). Medium goes on to the code review in the same turn; high waits for your go, and a rejected design ends the run. The code review runs context-isolated subagents against one shared diff packet: a fast implementation pass and the gstack security audit always, the lattice review only when the feature has a lattice design or context doc, and a background cross-model Codex pass on request (--codex) or on high-risk changes. Chat gets the verdict and each finding as one plain sentence; the code diffs go to report.md for the session that fixes them. A finding blocks only with a concrete failure scenario. When the review subject has a PR, it gathers the PR description and discussion for producer-side triage — never for the blind passes — and verifies that static-analysis findings (Wiz, Snyk, SonarCloud, CodeQL, …) were fixed, suppressed, or dismissed. Stack mode plans the reviews of a PR stack; a re-review (--delta) reviews only what changed since the last review and checks the earlier blockers.
